newsitem.title: CHINA: China car prices could fall 10 pct in 1997 - paper.
newsitem.headline: China car prices could fall 10 pct in 1997 - paper.

text.p: China's car prices, already battered by oversupply and weak demand, could fall 10 percent in 1997, the China Business Times on Sunday quoted a senior automobile official as saying.

Fierce competition in a weak market could mean manufacturers would have to slash prices to attract buyers, it quoted Zhang Xiaoyu, head of the automobile department of the Ministry of Machine-building Industry, as saying.

China has vowed to turn its car industry into a pillar of the national economy, but automakers have seen growth in demand fall far behind expectations and have been forced to fight for market share by slashing prices.
China's top 20 car producers would merge into three or four enterprise groups by the end of the century in order to face competition overseas, the Xinhua news agency said.
Several of China's top automakers were poised to acquire smaller companies, Xinhua said without naming any of the firms.

The Ministry of Machine-building Industry was considering accelerating the consolidation process by pressuring 30 small, loss-making plants to seek help from larger enterprises or file for bankruptcy, it said.
Some 116 automakers were registered with the ministry, Xinhua said.
The ministry urgently needed to prepare the industry for the increased foreign competition it would face if China successfuly joined the World Trade Organisation, it said.

China's long-stalled bid to join the World Trade Organisation appears to have made gains in recent months, and some government officials have suggested that an agreement on terms of its entry could be reached this year.
